solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: No time for food, getting fit

indicators.note: 'No time' tells the solver to take away the letter standing for time

parts.note: a table is the food served, as in 'she keeps a good table'
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone skips meals because they are too busy getting into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: TABLE loses its T to leave ABLE; 'table' for food is an old but standard sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capable or competent to do something is to be fit for it, a common synonym.

clue.text: Bird dropping head below black fence

indicators.note: the bird lets its first letter fall away
in a down entry one piece sitting below another simply comes after it

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a harrier is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A bird leaves its droppings on a dark-painted fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like bird mess but means losing: HARRIER drops its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is any structure that blocks passage, and a fence is one such obstruction.

clue.text: Old manuscript contains answer for tests

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
MS is the standard abbreviation for manuscript
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: An ancient document holds the solutions to some examination papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are formal written or oral assessments, which is exactly what tests of a student are.

clue.text: Hopeful dance with rogue's lamentable

indicators.note: something lamentable is in a sorry, wretched state, so the letters are in a mess

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An optimist's dance partner, a rascal, performs dreadfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', joining the fodder to its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been given heart and confidence feels optimistic, so the past participle works as an adjective here.

clue.text: Segregate criminal that's hunted in spring?

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the noun: the thing that is hunted

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the preceding word's letters are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Separating people unlawfully, the sort of thing pursued in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: children hunt chocolate eggs at Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter egg hunts are a springtime tradition in which children search gardens for hidden chocolate treats.

clue.text: Boxes jammed with European coins

indicators.note: the boxes are packed tight with something stuffed inside them

parts.note: crates are wooden boxes
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Packing cases are stuffed full of euro coinage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coins' looks like money but is the verb, as in coining a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a word or phrase is to invent it, which is to bring something new into existence.

clue.text: Brown horse possibly unseats knight

indicators.note: to unseat is to throw off, so a letter is knocked out

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, which possibly deadens feeling: a numb-er
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A bay horse throws its rider, a knight, from the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is drug slang for heroin; read 'number' as one that numbs, then remove N.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural earth pigment giving a dark brown colour used by painters.

clue.text: Star made off with millions in capital

indicators.note: something gone off has spoiled, so the letters are no longer in good order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A celebrity absconded with a fortune in some city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made off' reads as fled, but 'off' alone is the signal; 'with' just adds M.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital city of the Netherlands.

clue.text: I announced a little fair

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the letter or pronoun said out loud matches the organ of sight
some means a small amount

explanation.surface: Someone declares that they are only somewhat attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: EYESOME is a rare word meaning pleasant to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means beautiful, and something good to look at is pleasing to the sight.

clue.text: Holidays in Split close to beaches

parts.note: to split is to break

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of beaches

explanation.surface: Vacations taken in Split, the Croatian resort near the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Split is a Croatian port, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Short holidays are called breaks in British usage, as in a city break or weekend away.

clue.text: One providing relief for engineers upset about employer

indicators.note: the turned letters go around the other piece
upset in a down sense means turned over, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
a boss is the one who employs you

explanation.surface: Someone brings comfort to army engineers who are angry with their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief' suggests comfort but means raised design work; REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: An embosser raises patterns on a surface, and such raised designs are called relief work.

clue.text: Mess about with pint to get wasted

indicators.note: to mess about is to fiddle around, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fooling around with beer in order to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' suggests drunk; in the answer it means squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or time that has been squandered or used foolishly is described as misspent, as in a misspent youth.

clue.text: South African animal trainer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small grey antelope of southern Africa
second meaning: a sports shoe from the brand of that name

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a person who trains animals; 'trainer' is the British word for a sports shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The antelope gave its name to the sportswear company, whose running shoes are a well-known make of sneaker.

clue.text: I handled orders badly, being chicken

indicators.note: orders handled badly come out in the wrong sequence

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker confesses to fumbling instructions out of cowardice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' reads as cowardly but is the bird itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhode Island Red is an American breed of domestic fowl with reddish-brown plumage.

clue.text: Rise and speak at length about one with spirit

indicators.note: the speech goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to orate is to make a long formal speech
Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Stand up and make a long speech on a single drinker's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise in the sense of a river rising from its source is to begin or have its origin there.

clue.text: Play along with a group who perform acoustically

indicators.note: acoustically means as heard, so the sound of the phrase counts

parts.note: a theatre company is a group of performers

explanation.surface: A musician joins in with an unplugged band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acoustically' pretends to describe unamplified music.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany a singer is to play an instrumental part supporting them, joining in musically.

clue.text: Fine deceitful European captain of ship

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
lying means untruthful
a man from the Netherlands

explanation.surface: A dishonest Continental fellow in charge of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the Flying Dutchman is the doomed skipper condemned to sail forever, a name also given to his phantom vessel.

clue.text: Student leader to land head of house, perhaps

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front, so only its first letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter of land
the breadwinner heading a household is one example of a wage-earner

explanation.surface: A student president arrives to become head of a school house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that an earner is only one kind of household head.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying or acquiring a skill, so a pupil or trainee fits.

clue.text: Strip or uniform associated with northern outfit

parts.note: Uniform is the radio code word for U
N is the abbreviation for northern
a dress is an outfit

explanation.surface: Either take off your clothes or wear a uniform, a northern outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or uniform' is a nod: undress is also the term for a soldier's everyday uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to take off your clothes, which is exactly what removing garments means.

clue.text: Place for those with habits like The Priory?

definitions.text: Place for those with habits like The Priory?

parts.words: Place for those with habits like The Priory?
parts.note: surface reading: The Priory is a famous London rehab clinic for people with addictions
setter's reading: habits are the robes worn by nuns, and a priory is a religious house

explanation.walkthrough: The Priory clinic treats celebrities for drug and drink habits; the answer is a convent where habits are clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent housing women in religious orders is a religious community, much like a priory.

clue.text: One tip to lure in bloke with a smoke

indicators.note: these letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: a bloke is a man
Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very start, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of lure
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single piece of advice for attracting a man: offer him a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: I and L go inside MAN plus A; 'bloke' is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A manila is a cheroot or cigar from the Philippines, so it is a type of smoke.

clue.text: A motorway turn in China

parts.note: taken as written
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with 1 read as I
your go is your turn in a game

explanation.surface: Taking a highway exit somewhere in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from 'china plate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, and china in rhyming slang means a pal or mate.

clue.text: Drop swimmer as he's short and fat?

definitions.note: a description standing for the noun: a short, plump person

parts.note: to dump is to drop
a ling is a fish, a swimmer in crossword terms

explanation.surface: A swimming team axes a member for being small and overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' usually means a fish in crosswords; the question mark marks the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumpling is an affectionate name for a small, plump person, like the round pudding.

clue.text: Port and a shot downed by vacuous lads

indicators.note: a drink downed by someone ends up inside them
vacuous means empty, so the word loses its insides and keeps only its ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of lads
taken as written
to have a shot is to have a go

explanation.surface: Empty-headed young men knock back port and a shot of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' and 'shot' look like drinks; port is the definition, a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagos is Nigeria's largest city and a major seaport on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Where you put flowers around four is disturbing

definitions.note: used loosely: intrusive in a troubling way

indicators.note: the flower holder goes all round the number

parts.note: flowers go in a vase
Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: Arranging flowers around a foursome causes upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invasive intrudes where it is not wanted, so it can be troubling and upsetting.

clue.text: One dropping a line to get hold of Sturgeon?

definitions.text: One dropping a line to get hold of Sturgeon?

parts.words: One dropping a line to get hold of Sturgeon?
parts.note: surface reading: someone writing a note to contact Nicola Sturgeon, former First Minister of Scotland
setter's reading: casting a fishing line into the water to hook a sturgeon, a large fish

explanation.walkthrough: Capital S makes the fish look like the Scottish politician; to drop a line is both to write and to fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who fishes with rod and line is called this, and a sturgeon is one possible catch.

clue.text: Girls, you've changed in a severe way

indicators.note: the letters have been altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: Someone tells a group of young women they have altered drastically.
explanation.definitionFit: Grievously means seriously or gravely, as in grievously wounded, describing harm of a serious degree.

clue.text: Part of Dynasty elicits viewer's complaint

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, sitting within them

parts.note: spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A scene from the soap Dynasty draws complaints from TV viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: The viewer is an eye, not a television watcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an ailment of the organ that sees.
